literal: Before the learned, speaking what was learned so as to penetrate (their minds), and from those who are superior (in learning), acquiring their superior knowledge.
translation: Speak what you have learned before the learned so that it deeply penetrates their minds; and from those who are more learned than yourself, acquire their superior knowledge.
modern: கற்றவர்களின் முன்னே தான் கற்றவற்றை அவர்கள் மனதில் பதியுமாறு சொல்லி, தன்னைவிட அறிவில் சிறந்தவர்களிடமிருந்து அவர்கள் கற்ற சிறந்த அறிவைப் பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the dual duty of a scholar when interacting with an assembly of the learned. First, one must present what they have learned in a clear, convincing manner so that it is accepted and understood by other scholars. Second, one must remain open to learning, actively acquiring the deeper, superior knowledge possessed by those who are even more learned. This approach ensures both the effective sharing of one's own knowledge and the continuous growth of one's intellect without fear or arrogance.
